The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of lymphodepleting chemotherapy and xenogenic CAR-T cell therapy in dogs with spontaneous CD20+ lymphoma. Clinical trials at VROC help evaluate new cancer treatments for pets by assessing their safety, effectiveness, and potential side effects. ## Study title

Evaluation of xenogeneic CAR-T cell therapy for canine CD20+ B cell lymphoma

## Purpose of study

The current standard of care for canine B-cell lymphoma is a multi-agent (CHOP) chemotherapy protocol, which require weekly trips to the vet over approximately 5 months, costs $7k-12k, and puts 80-90% of dogs into remission for 9-12 months before relapse. Canine B-cell lymphoma resembles human non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, a cancer now successfully treated with Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells (CAR-T cells). In this study, LEAH Labs is sponsoring an pilot trial to test the safety of a CAR-T cell therapy product in dogs with B-cell lymphoma; with the hopes to find a more cost-effective and efficacious therapy for dogs with this disease.

# WCVM scientists seeking dogs with spreading cancer for clinical trial

Oncology researchers at the Western College of Veterinary Medicine (WCVM) are seeking dogs with spreading cancer for a clinical trial at the WCVM Veterinary Medical Centre.

May 20, 2024

#### Deciphering tumour heterogeneity through necropsy, imaging and transcriptomics in naturally occurring cancers in dogs.

One out of every four dogs is diagnosed with cancer, and sadly, half of those animals will die of the disease. Cancer's ability to spread is a major challenge, making it difficult to detect and treat effectively.

This clinical trial at the WCVM will explore potential solutions by using a new approach to studying cancer spreading in canine patients. 

WCVM researchers will study cancer spreading in pet dogs diagnosed with cancer using two tools: positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging, an advanced imaging technology, and RNA sequencing, a gene profiling method. 

The WCVM is the only Canadian veterinary college equipped with PET-CT technology. The state-of-the-art equipment allows allows human and veterinary cancer researchers at the University of Saskatchewan to offer this unique opportunity to pet owners.

#### What are the study's goals? 

The WCVM researchers aim to find a way to improve cancer detection and treatment by: 

  * exploring the role and benefits of PET-CT technology in understanding cancer spreading
  * assessing how different genes contribute to cancers in various parts of the body

#### What canine patients are eligible? 

The WCVM research team is seeking dogs with advanced-stage cancer. Eligible dogs must be healthy enough to undergo anesthesia and a PET-CT scan.

After their pet's death, owners will be asked to return to the WCVM Veterinary Medical Centre for a post-mortem examination (necropsy).  

#### What costs will the WCVM research team cover?  

Each dog enrolled in the clinical trial will undergo anesthesia and receive a PET-CT scan at no cost. In addition, there will be no charge for a post-mortem examination — a procedure that will allow the research team to gain a better understanding of the disease.

#### How can pet owners find out more about this clinical trial? 

If you own a dog that may be eligible for this trial, contact the study’s research team leader:

# Clinical Trials

### Welcome to a resource for information on current research trials in veterinary oncology.

Pet owners often ask us if we are aware of any CLINICAL TRIALS that may be available to their cat or dog who has been diagnosed with cancer. While there certainly are a number of studies occurring around the world, participation in a clinical trial can often be difficult, especially if the trial is going on in a hospital or clinic far away from your home.

Each clinical trial has very specific qualifications for participation that include everything from the breed and age of the participant to the life expectancy, weight and of course the type of cancer. Each study is very particular in its criteria for participation. Something else to take into consideration is that clinical trials are NOT always free. There may be fees to participate because grants may only cover a certain portion of the trial, and you may have to travel a long way to participate for several weeks or months perhaps.

## Clinical Research Trial Overview

Clinical trials may involve novel diagnostic methods or therapies including chemotherapy, radiation therapy, surgical procedures, hypo- or hyperthermia, immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy, among others. While most clinical research trials are conducted at colleges of veterinary medicine, a growing number of specialty referral practices are participating in clinical research. For some trials, all visits must occur at the trials institution or practice, but for others there are tests or procedures that could be performed at the general practice.

When discussing the possibility of participating in a clinical trial with pet owners, it is helpful to share that although “experimental,” or “investigational,” the safety and efficacy of new therapies and procedures have often been evaluated first in laboratory animals as well as normal dogs or cats, and the therapy is considered to be of potential benefit to the patient.

# Get free diagnostic testing for suspected canine transmissible cancer cases

16 October 2026

### A call out to our referring veterinary community:

If you suspect a case of canine transmissible venereal tumour (CTVT), contact the Transmissible Cancer Group at the Department of Veterinary Medicine, University of Cambridge. The team is running a national pilot study and offering PCR-based LINE-MYC diagnostic testing free of charge to vets across the UK.

The team accepts samples for DNA extraction in various formats and will return a definitive CTVT diagnostic result within a clinically useful timeframe. Submit a sample or get in touch with the team today!

Please see the TCG website to read more about how your case can get free CTVT diagnostic testing.

### Why Take Part?

Your participation will directly advance the understanding of CTVT transmission in the UK while helping establish faster, more reliable diagnostic pathways for veterinary practices nationwide.

Dr Andrea Strakova

Postdoctoral Scientist

### Background & Clinical Relevance

Canine transmissible venereal tumour is a unique infectious cancer transmitted via living cells during direct contact, such as mating, sniffing, or licking. Once diagnosed, CTVT is highly treatable with vincristine chemotherapy.

While CTVT was historically eradicated from the UK, incidence is currently rising due to the increased importation of dogs from endemic regions, particularly Eastern Europe. A recent case report confirmed active CTVT transmission within the UK for the first time in over 50 years.

Because UK prevalence has remained low for decades, many practitioners are unfamiliar with CTVT's presentation - especially atypical extragenital cases. Standard diagnostic methods (cytology, histology, and travel history) are not always conclusive. The LINE-MYC PCR assay provides the clarity needed for accurate diagnosis and prompt treatment.

In der vorliegenden Studie untersuchen wir die Sicherheit und Verträglichkeit der oralen Verabreichung von Vinorelbin bei Hunden mit Tumorerkrankungen. Ziel dieser frühen klinischen Phase-I-Studie ist es, eine geeignete Dosis zu bestimmen, die gut verträglich ist und keine schwerwiegenden Nebenwirkungen verursacht.

## Informationen zur Studie

Was ist Vinorelbin?

Vinorelbin ist ein Medikament gegen Krebs bei Menschen und Hunden. Studien zufolge können insbesondere Hunde mit Lymphom, histiozytärem Sarkom, Mastozytom und Lungenkarzinom von diesem Medikament profitieren. In der Tiermedizin steht es bislang jedoch nur intravenös zur Verfügung. Das kann bei einigen Tieren zu erhöhtem Stress, Angst oder Aggressivität führen und die Behandlung zusätzlich erschweren.

### Einschlusskriterien

  * Hunde mit einer Tumorerkrankung, bei denen eine Standardtherapie nicht mehr infrage kommt (z.B. grosse inoperable Tumore oder metastasierte Tumore) oder nicht durchgeführt werden kann (z.B. Kosten)
  * Hunde mit gutem Allgemeinzustand
  *  Körpergewicht > 5 kg

### Vorteile

Ihr Tier erhält eine einfache Therapieoption, die möglicherweise wirksam ist. Gleichzeitig helfen Sie dabei, eine neue Therapieform für zukünftige Patienten zu etablieren.

Ein Teil der Kosten wird durch eine Stiftung übernommen.

## Hintergrundinformationen

In der Humanmedizin ist die orale Gabe von Vinorelbin längst etabliert, da sie für die Patientinnen und Patienten deutlich bequemer ist. Ältere Patienten profitieren davon besonders.

Auch bei Hunden könnte eine orale Chemotherapie den Klinikbesuch vereinfachen und stressfreier gestalten – sowohl für das Tier als auch für den Halter.

## Was ist das Ziel?

# Lattice- oder SBRT Strahlentherapie bei grossen Tumoren

Hunde, Katzen |

  Onkologie |

 Studienteilnahme möglich

Zuletzt aktualisiert am 8. Juli 2025

Die Lattice-Strahlentherapie ist eine innovative Form der Krebsbestrahlung zur Behandlung grosser, schwer therapierbarer Tumoren. Dabei wird der Tumor nicht gleichmässig, sondern punktuell in einem gitterförmigen Muster bestrahlt (engl. „Lattice“).

## Informationen zur Studie

Bei Hunden mit grossen, nicht operierbaren Tumoren wird oft eine besondere Form der Bestrahlung eingesetzt, um den Tumor zu verkleinern. Eine übliche Methode ist die sogenannte stereotaktische Body Radiotherapy (SBRT), die je nach Tumortyp diesen deutlich schrumpfen lässt. Eine neue Methode, die sogenannte «Lattice-Bestrahlung», zeigt in bis zu 87 % der Fälle bessere Ergebnisse. Dabei wird der Tumor nicht gleichmässig, sondern gezielt an bestimmten Stellen mit hoher Dosis bestrahlt – ähnlich einem Gittermuster. Das kann den Tumor nicht nur direkt stärker schädigen, sondern auch das Immunsystem gegen den Krebs aktivieren.

### Einschlusskriterien

Hunde mit grossen, inoperablen Tumoren; oder wenn die Strahlentherapie einer Operation vorgezogen wird.

### Vorteile

Diese Methoden ermöglichen eine intensive Tumorbehandlung bei gleichzeitig geringer Belastung des gesunden Gewebes – insbesondere bei grossen Tumoren, die mit herkömmlicher Strahlentherapie schwer behandelbar wären.

## Hintergrundinformationen

In dieser klinischen Studie vergleichen wir die beiden Methoden (SBRT und Lattice-Strahlentherapie) direkt miteinander. Man vermutet eine unterschiedliche Aktivierung des Immunsystems, das die Tumorzerstörung unterstützen kann.

Image

## Was ist das Ziel?

Ziel ist es, herauszufinden, welche Methode den Tumor besser verkleinert und wie sich beide auf das Immunsystem und gesunde Gewebe auswirken.

## Was passiert bei der Studie?

Bei einer Studienteilnahme wird entweder ein SBRT- oder ein Lattice-Bestrahlungsplan erstellt.

Die Auswahl wird dem Zufall überlassen (d. h. randomisiert), die Behandlung findet aber auf jeden Fall an fünf aufeinanderfolgenden Tagen statt.

Falls der Tumor gut zugänglich ist und es für das Tier kein zusätzliches Risiko bedeutet, werden vor der ersten und bei der letzten Bestrahlung sowie bei der 3-Wochen-Nachkontrolle kleine Tumorproben entnommen, um die Wirkung auf das Immunsystem zu untersuchen.

Zum Forschungsteam gehört Dr. Sergejs Unterkirhers, Leiter der Stereotaxie am Institut für Radiotherapie Zürich, Klinik Hirslanden.

Cats and dogs are the most popular companion animal species in New Zealand so it’s no surprise both feature prominently in recently approved research projects.Image: cat

### Could a novel drug combination combat cancer in cats?

Three Massey University researchers will lead a trial of a novel drug combination administered to cats with mouth cancer that could pave the way for a revolution in the treatment of animal cancer.

Oral squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) are common in both humans and cats. Professor John Munday, Associate Professor Keren Dittmer and Dr Thomas Odom are trialling a novel drug ‘cocktail’ to block a cancer regulation pathway. As this pathway is important to the growth and spread of cancer, blocking the pathway is expected to prevent cancer progression.

Six cats with inoperable oral SCCs will be carefully monitored to confirm the safety of this novel treatment, which the researchers hope will also reduce cancer progression in this initial study.

# 臨床研究情報

## 臨床試験について

本院で行っている、もしくは行う予定の臨床試験についてです。臨床試験とは、安全で有効となりうることが期待される医薬品もしくは医療機器を用いた治療です。 飼い主様への十分な説明と、飼い主様の同意の下で実施します。現在実施している臨床試験は以下の通りです。

  * 慢性腸症罹患犬に対する乳酸菌およびオリゴ糖の有効性に関する臨床試験
  * 犬の組織球性肉腫に対する抗PD-1抗体を用いた臨床試験
  * 犬猫の固形腫瘍に対するがんオルガノイドスクリーニング検査に基づく分子標的薬投与の安全性と有効性検証のための臨床試験
  * ネコの移行上皮癌に対するラパチニブの獣医師主導臨床試験
  * 犬の膀胱・尿道移行上皮癌および前立腺癌に対する臨床試験
  * 犬の膀胱癌に対するIDO1阻害剤の臨床試験
## 犬の組織球性肉腫に対する抗PD-1抗体を用いた臨床試験

犬の組織球性肉腫は極めて悪性の癌であり、急速に進行することが知られていますが有効な治療法は確立されていません。
近年、人においてPD-1という分子を標的とした抗体薬を用いた免疫療法が、がん患者の一部で有効であることがわかってきました。また犬においても山口大学のこれまでの臨床試験によりある種のがんに対して効果があることが明らかとなりました。
そこで、あらたに犬の組織球肉腫に対する犬PD-1に対する抗体薬の有効性と安全性を調べるために、臨床試験を実施しています。なお、この試験は2026年7月に当センター臨床試験委員会において倫理的承認を受けております。

# 犬の口腔内悪性黒色腫を対象とした抗イヌ PD-1 抗体の国内治験開始のお知らせ

報道機関　各位

**2026 年 10 月 6 日**

日本全薬工業株式会社（本社：福島県郡山市、代表取締役社長：福井寿一）は、このたび、犬の口腔内悪性黒色腫を対象とした抗イヌ PD-1 抗体の有効性および安全性を評価する国内治験を開始いたしましたので、お知らせいたします。

## 犬の悪性黒色腫（メラノーマ）について

悪性黒色腫は犬にもみられる悪性腫瘍の一つであり、特に口腔内に発生する症例では局所浸潤や遠隔転移を生じやすく、予後不良となることが知られています。

## 抗 PD-1 抗体について

抗 PD-1 抗体は、PD-1 を標的とする抗体であり、ヒト医療では複数のがんに対する治療薬として実用化されています。今回使用する治験薬は、日本全薬工業株式会社が国立大学法人山口大学との共同研究を通じて開発を進めてきた、イヌ PD-1 を標的とする抗体（抗イヌ PD-1 抗体）※1です。

## Clinical Trials Now Enrolling

#### CALL FOR PATIENTS: Clinical Trial for Soft Tissue Sarcoma in Dogs

Study Title: Feasibility and dose-optimization clinical trial of local immunotherapy for solid tumors in canine cancer patients

Eligibility: Any dog weighing 5kg or above with at least one cutaneous soft tissue sarcoma lesion that is greater than 1.7cm in diameter is eligible to enroll. All dogs that meet the study criteria will receive the study drug (no placebo) followed by surgical removal of the tumor 1 week later.

Study Purpose: This clinical trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and biological effects of a newly designed immunotherapy. Specifically, the study is evaluating the injection of investigational T-cell engagers (TCEs) directly into tumors (intratumorally) in canine patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS). TCEs are engineered antibodies that physically connect T cells to cancer cells by targeting specific markers (CD3 or CD28 on T cells, and B7-H3 or PD-L1 on cancer cells), triggering the immune system to destroy tumor cells.

#### Safety Measures, Risks, and Potential Benefits

While procedures like blood draws, ultrasound, anesthesia, and surgery carry standard medical risks, the investigational TCEs also carry the potential risks of temporary discomfort, minor bleeding, redness, and irritation at the injection site. Although this study seeks to reduce these risks through careful selection of the TCEs and the intratumoral doses to be used, these and other side effects could occur including overactive immune responses/allergic reactions, gastro-intestinal upset, and other potential unforeseen adverse reactions. To mitigate these risks, all enrolled dogs receive pre-treatment diphenhydramine (Benadryl) to reduce allergic reactions, undergo overnight hospital monitoring following injection, and receive carefully adjusted dosages across patient cohorts.

While enrolled dogs may not receive direct health benefits from this trial, their participation will help advance the development of vital cancer treatments for both dogs and humans. Participation in this study will include a $1,500 credit towards surgical removal of the tumor at VRCCO, along with full coverage for any ICU stays, study-related blood work, and medications required due to study participation.

หน้าที่และความรับผิดชอบหลัก

  * มีความรู้พื้นฐานด้านศัลยกรรม โดยจะจัดให้มีการฝึกอบรมขั้นตอน การผ่าตัดทำหมันหมันสุนัขและแมว เพศผู้และเพศเมีย ตามวิธีการที่ทางคลินิกกำหนด และตามเป้าหมายการผ่าตัดทำหมันต่อวัน รวมถึงรักษาสัตว์ป่วยหรือบาดเจ็บ ตามความจำเป็น
  * สังเกต วิเคราะห์ และแก้ไขปัญหาที่เกิดขึ้นภายในคลินิกในแต่ละวัน

  * ทำงานร่วมกันเป็นทีม พร้อมช่วยเหลืองานอื่นๆ ตามที่หัวหน้างานกำหนด และตามความเหมาะสม แม้อยู่นอกเหนือจากขอบเขตหน้าที่โดยตรง

คุณสมบัติ

  * สำเร็จการศึกษาระดับปริญญาตรี สาขาสัตวแพทยศาสตร์ และมีใบประกอบวิชาชีพสัตวแพทย์ (มีหรือไม่มีประสบการณ์ก็ได้ ยินดีรับนักศึกษาจบใหม่ โดยผู้มีประสบการณ์ด้านการรักษาจะได้รับการพิจารณาเป็นพิเศษ)
  * สามารถวินิจฉัยและรักษาโรคทางอายุรกรรมพื้นฐานได้ และ มีความรู้พื้นฐานด้านศัลยกรรม โดยทางคลินิกจะจัดให้มีการฝึกอบรมขั้นตอนการผ่าตัดทำหมันตามมาตรฐานที่กำหนด
  * มีความเมตตา รักสัตว์ มีใจรักงานบริการ และสามารถทำงานเป็นทีมได้อย่างมีประสิทธิภาพ
  * สามารถทำงานภายใต้ความกดดัน และรับมือกับสถานการณ์ฉุกเฉินได้
  * มีความตรงต่อเวลา ขยัน สามารถยืดหยุ่นเวลาการทำงานได้ และออกหน่อยนอกสถานที่ได้
  * มีทักษะการสื่อสารภาษาอังกฤษในระดับพอใช้ และสามารถทำงานร่วมกับทีมงานที่มีความหลากหลายได้ดี

## Abstract

### Background

Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common histologic subtype of lymphoma in dogs. Although using cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone (CHOP) chemotherapy is the standard treatment, outcomes remain suboptimal, emphasizing the need for novel therapeutic strategies.

### Hypothesis/Objectives

Evaluate the feasibility and potential therapeutic benefit of adoptive immunotherapy using ex vivo-expanded cytokine-activated anti-tumor lymphocytes (CATLs) in dogs with DLBCL treated using CHOP chemotherapy and an autologous tumor vaccine.

## Abstract

This review summarizes the findings of veterinary clinical trials on immunogene therapy published between 2017 and 2024. Various tumor types, including melanoma (canine and feline), mastocytoma (canine), mammary adenocarcinoma (canine), osteosarcoma (canine), and sarcoid (equine), were treated using diverse strategies. Non-viral vectors were predominantly used to deliver genes encoding tumor-associated antigens, cytokines, or suicide enzymes. Among these non-viral methods, electrotransfer was the most commonly employed technique for introducing therapeutic genes into cells. Generally, these procedures resulted in minimal or no adverse side effects, and treated animals often showed significant improvements, such as enhanced quality of life, delayed or suppressed tumor recurrence or metastasis, and increased survival times. Some of these innovative approaches hold great potential as adjunct therapies to standard treatments. The promising outcomes from immunogene therapy studies in companion animals strongly support their application in veterinary oncology and provide valuable preclinical data (including safety assessments and proof-of-concept studies) for analogous human clinical trials.

Certain forms of cancer have the ability to spread to other sites in the body which are often far from the original site. In the majority of these cases this happens when cancer cells enter the blood or lymph vessels and are then carried to other organs. Cancers with this type of behaviour are considered malignant. Often, it is the spread of a cancer that causes the greatest problems. When a cancer has spread in this fashion, it is said to have metastasized. Some cancers lack the ability to metastasize, but may cause significant damage due to growth and invasion into local tissues. Tumours that do not metastasize are generally considered non-invasive and thus are termed benign. Tumour is a general term for cancer whether it is benign (“good cancer”) or malignant (“bad cancer”). Oncology is the branch of medicine dedicated to the study of cancer, and the doctors treating people with cancer are called Oncologists and Oncology nurses. # Clinical Trials for Dogs with Cancer

Links last verified: August 20, 2026

## Explore Current Research Trials in Canine Oncology

When a beloved dog is diagnosed with cancer, many families ask whether a clinical trial may provide an additional option. Canine oncology studies are conducted throughout the United States and around the world, but identifying an appropriate trial, and participating in one, can sometimes be challenging.

Each clinical trial has specific eligibility requirements.

These may include: 

  * A dog’s breed
  * Age
  * Weight
  * Overall health
  * Life expectancy
  * Cancer type
  * Cancer stage
  * Previous care
  * ...and other medical factors

Meeting a study’s general description does not guarantee acceptance. Pet parents should speak directly with the research team and their veterinary care provider to determine whether a trial may be appropriate for their dog.

It is also important to understand that clinical trials are not always free.

Research funding may cover only certain tests, medications, procedures, or appointments. Families may still be responsible for additional veterinary expenses, travel, lodging, and repeated visits over several weeks or months, especially when a study is located far from home.

The following links are intended to help pet parents and veterinary professionals find information about current canine oncology trials being conducted throughout the United States and, in some cases, internationally.

We encourage families to carefully review each study’s eligibility requirements, location, potential costs, time commitment, and possible benefits and risks with their veterinary team.

Terapi inovatif berasaskan sel stem mesenchymal menyasarkan tumor peringkat akhir dengan jenis kanser tertentu oleh anjing dan kucing ini djangka akan menjalankan ujian klinikal melalui Hospital Veterinar Universiti (UVH), UPM.

“By the time we were setting up this clinical trial, this was the first public Oncology clinical trial in Kenya. We put the University of Nairobi on the global map,” Prof Oyugi added.
